question: A sum of ₹2,500 amounts to ₹2,809 in 2 years at a certain rate of interest per annum, compounded annually. The rate of interest per annum is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Amount to Principal = 2809 / 2500

Since the time period is 2 years, we take the square root of the ratio to find the multiplying factor for 1 year.

Multiplying factor for 1 year = √(2809 / 2500) = 53 / 50

Interest earned in 1 year = 53 − 50 = 3 parts on a base principal of 50 parts.

Rate of interest = (3 / 50) × 100 = 6%

**∴ The correct answer is 6%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹2500

Amount (A) = ₹2809

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + R / 100)T

 
 ₹2500
 Principal (P)
 
 
 ₹2809
 Amount (A)

 
• 
 

 
 Time = 2 years
 Rate = R% p.a.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2809 = 2500(1 + R / 100)²

⇒ 2809 / 2500 = (1 + R / 100)²

⇒ (53 / 50)² = (1 + R / 100)²

Taking the square root on both sides:

⇒ 53 / 50 = 1 + R / 100

⇒ R / 100 = 53 / 50 − 1

⇒ R / 100 = 3 / 50

⇒ R = (3 / 50) × 100

⇒ R = 6%

**∴ The correct answer is 6%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

SI vs CI Difference (for 2 years)

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for exactly 2 years on the same principal is given by the formula D = P(R / 100)².

Half-Yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the annual rate is halved (R / 2) and the time period in terms of conversion cycles is doubled (2T).

Rule of 72

A popular shortcut rule to estimate the number of years required to double the invested money at a given annual compound interest rate is T ≈ 72 ÷ Rate%.
